subtype: Approach: saying no and walking to a trusted adult [Action]
passage: Come closer, little one; your grandfather Tenzin wants to tell you what your cousin Trisha did when she was ten. A man near the school gate told her to come with him to see something. Trisha said, "No." She stepped back, kept a scooter's length away, and walked over to the security guard near the entrance. She told the guard exactly what the man had said, and the guard stood beside her until the man had gone. That evening she told her parents too, and we all sat and listened until she had finished. I was proud, but even more than that, I was relieved.

qa.q: Who did Trisha tell at the gate?
qa.a: Trisha told the guard at the gate.

qa.q: What was Tenzin feeling when he heard about that evening?
qa.a: He felt proud and even more relieved that Trisha was safe.

qa.q: What choices did Trisha make that kept her safe?
qa.a: She said no, kept her distance and walked to the guard, then told her parents, so adults knew straight away.

qa.q: How might the guard have seen Trisha coming toward him?
qa.a: The guard probably saw a child asking for protection, and stood beside her until the man had gone.

grounding: A girl refuses to go anywhere with a stranger, keeps distance, tells the gate guard, then her parents.
